title: The Cracked Floor
bodyText: A hairline crack has appeared in the bunker's concrete sub-floor. Water is seeping through — dark, metallic-smelling. Aris Thorne runs his fingers along the crack with the precision of a man who designed shelters like this before the war. 'This is bad,' he says quietly. 'I know exactly how bad this can get.'

choices.text: Let Aris assess the damage fully.

title: The Overwork
bodyText: Aris hasn't slept in three days. His hands shake as he mixes concrete, but his work is flawless. Other survivors whisper that he's killing himself. When approached, he snaps: 'I designed these shelters. Every crack is my fault. Let me fix it.'

choices.text: Force Aris to rest. The repair holds. It's good enough.
Let him push through. He knows what he's doing.

title: The Resolution
bodyText: The crack is sealed. Aris stands in front of his work, one hand pressed against the concrete. 'My daughter would have turned seven today,' he says. 'She would have been proud of this.' He turns away from the wall. Some cracks can't be filled with concrete.

title: The Signal
bodyText: Maya Lin freezes at the radio console. Her hand hovers over the frequency dial. 'That pattern,' she whispers. 'That's Emergency Action Message format. Standard military. But the voice — ' She presses the headphones tighter. 'The voice is my brother's. Jakob was stationed at Checkpoint Kilo.'

choices.text: Help Maya trace the signal to its source.

title: The Death Loop
bodyText: The signal source is found: an automated transmitter running on a failing battery. Jakob recorded this three years ago. He's been dead since Year 1. Maya removes the headphones. Her face is completely still. 'He was alone,' she says. 'He died alone, talking to a radio.'

choices.text: Help Maya channel her grief into saving others through the radio.
Give Maya space. She needs to process this alone.

title: The Broadcast
bodyText: Maya sits at the radio console, her hand steady on the transmitter. 'This is Free Radio, broadcasting from somewhere the ash hasn't reached yet,' she says. Her voice carries across every frequency. 'If you can hear this, you're not alone.' Somewhere, in a dozen bunkers, a dozen survivors press their headphones tighter.

title: The Refugee Mass
bodyText: A woman and two children huddle in the airlock, their dosimeter readings screaming. They have twenty minutes of safe exposure left. Captain Vance stands at the hatch, arms crossed. 'Rations are tight,' he says flatly. 'Every mouth we add shortens our survival window by days. The math is clear.' The mother is crying.

title: The Command Decision
bodyText: Vance's tactical assessment is correct: accepting the refugees will strain food supplies by 15%. But the bunker has room. The youngest child — maybe four years old — is shivering so hard her teeth are chattering. Vance won't look at her. He's staring at the inventory ledger instead.

choices.text: Admit the refugees. Override Vance's recommendation.
Turn them away. Vance's cold math is correct.

title: The Treaty
bodyText: Vance removes his service pistol and sets it on the table. 'I spent ten years following orders that turned me into something I didn't recognize,' he says. 'Today, I'm giving a different order.' He extends his hand — to a Militia commander, to a Garrison defector, to anyone willing to stop fighting long enough to survive.

title: The ARS Diagnosis
bodyText: Dr. Rostov reviews the bloodwork with clinical detachment. 'Terminal Acute Radiation Syndrome,' she announces. 'Twelve days. Maybe fourteen with aggressive treatment.' The patient is someone she's treated before — someone she knows by name. Her voice doesn't shake. Her hands do.

choices.text: Review the treatment options with Elena.

title: The Triage
bodyText: Elena lays out the cost in a monotone: 'Eighty percent of our remaining medical supplies. Antibiotics, morphine, iodine, surgical kits — almost everything we have left to save a single patient with low survival odds.' She pauses. 'The mathematics is clear.' The patient is watching her. Waiting.

choices.text: Save the patient. Every life matters regardless of cost.
Trust Elena's clinical judgment. Let them pass peacefully.

title: The Remedy
bodyText: In the quiet of the medical bay, Elena holds a vial up to the lantern light. The liquid inside glows faintly green — a compound derived from the spores of the Overgrown Botanical Nursery. 'The Ash Rot Remedy,' she whispers. 'It took me three years to synthesize. It will cure chronic fallout lung rot. Permanently.' She labels the vial. One word: 'HOPE.'

title: The Defector's Story
bodyText: A Garrison soldier stumbles into the airlock, uniform torn, rifle empty. 'I couldn't do it anymore,' they gasp. 'The executions. The tribute collections. Colonel Voss ordered us to burn a settlement that was three days late on food quotas. I — I walked away. They're probably hunting me.' They hand over a data chip. 'Patrol routes. Supply schedules. Everything I know.'

choices.text: Welcome the defector. Their intel is invaluable.
Take the intel but turn them away. Too dangerous.

title: The Prophet Sighting
bodyText: A traveler at the Grain Exchange describes something impossible: 'I saw The Vessel — the Cult's prophet. Walking through Reactor Site 4 like it was a garden. No suit. No protection. Just walking. The Geiger counter was off the scale and they were just... walking. Smiling.' The traveler's hands are shaking. 'They said to tell everyone: the Clear World is coming.'

choices.text: Send someone to verify. If it's true, we need to know.

title: The Council Invitation
bodyText: A Militia courier arrives with a handwritten letter. 'The Ash Militia Council requests the presence of a representative from your shelter at our monthly assembly. Topics: mutual defense pact, water purification technology exchange, and the establishment of a formal trade route. Food and lodging provided. Weapons checked at the door.' The letter is signed by twelve different hands.

choices.text: Send a representative. This could be the start of something.
Decline. We can't afford to send anyone right now.
